question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{126}$ be a random sample of size $n=126$ from a population with a population mean $\mu =5$ and population standard deviation $\sigma =84.$ Find an approximation for $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>3.5).$ *Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.03\,$$\,0.04\,$$\,0.05\,$
$\,-1.2\,$ $\,0.1093\,$ $\,0.1075\,$ $\,0.1056\,$
$\,-1.1\,$ $\,0.1292\,$ $\,0.1271\,$ $\,0.1251\,$
$\,-1.0\,$ $\,0.1515\,$ $\,0.1492\,$ $\,0.1469\,$

$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.4207\,$ $\,0.4168\,$ $\,0.4129\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4602\,$ $\,0.4562\,$ $\,0.4522\,$
$\,0.0\,$ $\,0.5000\,$ $\,0.5040\,$ $\,0.5080\,$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with a population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n=126,\,\mu =5,\,\sigma =84.
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(5,\frac{{84}^{2}}{126}) \\  & ∼N(5,56).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>3.5).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>3.5) & =1-P(|\overset{―}{X}|<3.5) \\  & =1-P(-3.5<\overset{―}{X}<3.5) \\  & =1-P(\frac{-3.5-5}{\sqrt{56}}<Z<\frac{3.5-5}{\sqrt{56}}) \\  & ≈1-P(-1.14<Z<-0.20) \\  & =1-(P(Z<-0.20)-P(Z<-1.14)) \\  & =1+Φ(-1.14)-Φ(-0.20).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.14)=0.1271, \\ Φ(-0.20)=0.4207.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>3.5) & =1+Φ(-1.14)-Φ(-0.20) \\  & =1+0.1271-0.4207 \\  & =0.7064.\end{aligned}
$$
